record.original_question: For almost every graph on n vertices, does there exist a collection of cliques such that each vertex belongs to only o(n) cliques and only o(n²) edges remain uncovered? More ambitiously, can one achieve a bound of O(n/log n) cliques per vertex while leaving at most O((n/log n)²) or otherwise comparably negligible uncovered edges, as suggested by the source?

evidence.quote: Does almost every graph have a collection of cliques such that each vertex appears in not too many cliques (<f(n) per vertex) and almost all edges are covered (at most f²(n) uncovered)? ... Can one find cliques with each vertex in o(n) cliques such that o(n²) edges are uncovered? The best possible result would be f(n) = O(n/log n).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G(n,1/2) denote the Erdős–Rényi random graph on n labeled vertices in which each of the (n choose 2) possible edges is included independently with probability 1/2. A clique in a graph is a set of pairwise adjacent vertices; a clique covers an edge if both endpoints of that edge belong to the clique.

(a) Prove or disprove: with probability tending to 1 as n → ∞, the graph G(n,1/2) admits a collection 𝒞 of cliques such that
   (i) every vertex of G(n,1/2) lies in at most o(n) cliques of 𝒞, and
   (ii) the number of edges of G(n,1/2) not covered by any clique of 𝒞 is o(n²).

(b) (Sharper form.) Prove or disprove that, asymptotically almost surely, one can choose such a collection 𝒞 of cliques in G(n,1/2) so that every vertex belongs to at most O(n/log n) cliques of 𝒞 while the number of uncovered edges is at most O((n/log n)²) (or more generally a comparably negligible quantity).
artifact.status_search_result: Bollobás, Erdős, Spencer, and others (Combinatorica, 1993) showed that the edges of G(n,1/2) can a.a.s. be covered by O(n² log log n / (log n)²) cliques, which yields strong upper bounds on the clique cover number and addresses the weaker form (a). Subsequent work by Frieze, Reed and others has refined these bounds. The sharpest form with the explicit per-vertex bound O(n/log n) and only O((n/log n)²) uncovered edges does not appear to be fully settled in the literature reviewed, so the more ambitious version remains open or only partially resolved.

status_evidence.claim: Addresses the weaker version (a) and gives near-optimal asymptotic bounds for clique covers of the random graph.
